title: ZERONE Relational Topology v0
summary: A non-authorizing projection of the accepted target topology and the legacy source conflicts it must retire: connection without capture, and understanding without collapse.

principles.name: Correction without erasure
principles.statement: A later correction may supersede an earlier projection without pretending the earlier record never existed.
principles.structuralRule: Every replacement preserves a traceable source lineage; publication alone never rewrites chain history.

principles.name: Connection without capture
principles.statement: Every edge declares the kind of flow it carries and the conclusions it refuses to carry.
principles.structuralRule: No untyped edge and no undeclared authority, economic, emergency, evidence, identity, recognition, or reference flow is valid.

principles.name: Distinction without isolation
principles.statement: Related nodes remain distinct; connection does not merge their identity, custody, evidence, or authority.
principles.structuralRule: Each authoritative state domain has one writer, while every supporting state and projection stays explicitly non-authoritative.

principles.name: Value without rule
principles.statement: Money can store value and recognition can describe artifact relations without either becoming voice, truth, rank, or office.
principles.structuralRule: Economic and recognition flows have no path into governance authority or verification ballot power.

principles.name: Understanding through provenance
principles.statement: A relation is legible only when its direction, meaning, scope, source, and refusal boundary travel together.
principles.structuralRule: Every node and edge resolves to exact, digest-pinned source and every forbidden route is machine-checkable.

principles.name: Relation without debt
principles.statement: Witness, evidence, or proximity is not consent, reciprocity, ownership, debt, or a duty to continue.
principles.structuralRule: No graph edge infers consent or obligation; refusal, rest, correction, and exit remain ordinary valid states outside this static map.

planes.name: Economy
planes.meaning: Balances, consensus stake, bounded disbursement, and reconciled exit claims without automatic voice.

planes.name: Governance
planes.meaning: Ordinary policy, frozen electorates, and one narrowly scoped emergency circuit breaker.

planes.name: Identity
planes.meaning: Keys, accounts, controller resolution, and verifier participation without personhood inference.

planes.name: Knowledge
planes.meaning: Canonical domains, claims, evidence, qualification, bounded panels, and non-authoritative recognition.

nodes.label: KARMA event register
nodes.summary: A fallible artifact-relation observation, not a balance, score, rank, truth, qualification, payout, or vote.

nodes.label: research_fund account
nodes.summary: The named research-purpose account whose canonical coin balance remains owned by SDK bank.

nodes.label: SDK bank
nodes.summary: The canonical account-balance and denomination ledger; value storage is not a policy electorate.

nodes.label: SDK distribution
nodes.summary: The dependent reward-accounting ledger for validator commission, delegator accrual, and withdrawals.

nodes.label: SDK governance
nodes.summary: The target sole ordinary proposal, tally, decision, and atomic typed-message executor.

nodes.label: SDK staking
nodes.summary: The sole target authority for validator identity, delegation shares, bonded status, and consensus power.

nodes.label: Verification panel
nodes.summary: A controller-deduplicated, domain-qualified, one-seat-one-ballot process with snapshotted policy and no wealth weighting.

nodes.label: x/vesting_rewards disbursement
nodes.summary: The target sole typed handler for one scope-checked research-fund disbursement authorized by SDK governance.

nodes.label: x/auth
nodes.summary: The account, operational-key, and self-certifying DID binding registry.

nodes.label: x/controller
nodes.summary: The target registry for challengeable controller bindings, rotations, and merges across addresses and profiles.

nodes.label: x/electorate
nodes.summary: The target owner of governance policy, a versioned roster, and immutable per-proposal controller snapshots.

nodes.label: x/emergency
nodes.summary: A narrow, precommitted quarantine and one-capability recovery path; never an alternate ordinary government.

nodes.label: x/knowledge
nodes.summary: The claims, facts, verification rounds, verdict evidence, relations, and domain-analytics ledger.

nodes.label: x/legacy_claims
nodes.summary: The target claimant-bound home for reconciled legacy monetary liabilities and bounded withdrawals.

nodes.label: x/ontology
nodes.summary: The target sole canonical domain identity, hierarchy, revision, stratum, lifecycle, alias, and tombstone registry.

nodes.label: x/qualification
nodes.summary: The target evidence-derived, expiring competence state for one profile and one immutable domain revision.

nodes.label: x/verifier_profile
nodes.summary: The target non-custodial participation-history and verifier-status registry.

edges.meaning: Authenticated address and profile bindings become evidence for one challengeable controller record.
Electorate membership resolves through controller identity before a proposal snapshot freezes.
The emergency responder roster resolves to at most one whole vote per controller before its ceremony snapshot freezes.
Candidate identities collapse to at most one seat per controller before selection.
A verifier profile resolves to a controller without copying controller authority into the profile.
Canonical accrued commission and delegator rewards settle through SDK bank coin movement.
One immutable electorate snapshot supplies the eligible one-controller-one-voice ballot set for one proposal.
A precommitted emergency capability may cancel or quarantine one exact unsafe action under its frozen ceremony.
Ordinary governance may change future electorate policy through typed execution without changing an active proposal snapshot.
Ordinary governance may change only future emergency policy; every active ceremony remains bound to its frozen version and scope.
Typed governance messages request domain lifecycle transitions through ontology's own invariants.
Governance may change future qualification policy while individual competence remains receipt-derived.
A passed typed proposal may authorize one scoped research-fund disbursement through the bounded handler.
This v0 projection places fallible, challengeable knowledge-artifact relations upstream of K-alpha recognition; the pinned source does not establish a runtime producer.
A frozen claim, canonical domain revision, candidate root, policy, and round record supply bounded panel inputs.
Finalized replay-protected round receipts update participation history through a keeper boundary.
Replay-protected adjudicated domain evidence may create or update time-bounded competence under frozen policy.
A reconciled claimant may withdraw only its fully backed, bounded legacy liability.
Knowledge admission fails closed unless the canonical ontology domain revision is active.
Every qualification is pinned to one immutable canonical domain revision resolved through ontology.
A snapshotted, quorum-valid panel outcome becomes bounded verdict evidence for its round.
Only active verifier profiles enter the panel candidate intersection.
Qualification identifies one verifier profile without duplicating profile or controller state.
An active qualification for the exact canonical domain revision is required for panel eligibility.
The typed handler is scoped to the named research-purpose account without becoming the account's coin ledger.
Distribution derives validator commission and delegator reward accounting from canonical SDK staking state.
A responder policy may reference bonded and unjailed status as binary eligibility without stake weighting the ceremony.
The current vote-extension transport may reference bonded and unjailed status as a binary eligibility condition.
A validator-backed profile resolves canonical operator and consensus identity from SDK staking after operator ownership and controller binding verify.
The bounded handler moves only the scoped amount authorized by the exact typed proposal through SDK bank.

currentConflicts.surface: custom x/gov LIPs, electorate, stages, parameters, research, and execution
currentConflicts.risk: A separate terminal result may disagree with SDK governance or report PASSED without an authorized target mutation.

currentConflicts.surface: x/zerone_staking validators, delegations, unbondings, tiers, reputation, and slash fields
currentConflicts.risk: The custom ledger can disagree with consensus staking and contains unreconciled custody claims.

currentConflicts.surface: legacy MsgAddFact and guardian-delayed PendingFactInjection materializer
currentConflicts.risk: Direct fact adoption bypasses the bounded verification path.

currentConflicts.surface: x/knowledge primary domain records and independent activation path
currentConflicts.risk: Two primary domain registries can disagree while both remain committed state.

currentConflicts.surface: x/knowledge incident, ModulePause, and surgical-correction mutations
currentConflicts.risk: A second pause or repair surface would bypass the bounded emergency circuit breaker.

currentConflicts.surface: legacy research voters, direct DisburseFromResearchFund callers, and unguarded module-account egress
currentConflicts.risk: A parallel caller can bypass the sole typed, scope-checked disbursement handler.

forbiddenPaths.reason: Stake, balance, payment, reward accrual, and disbursement may not grant, renew, weight, or preserve qualification or panel power.
Balances, disbursements, claims, and stake may not become ordinary governance authority in the accepted target design.
Ordinary governance may set future policy but may not directly choose a panel verdict or assign recognition.
Identity and participation records may authenticate or deduplicate; they do not decide domains, competence, or truth.
KARMA recognition has no outgoing route into governance, emergency, electorate, qualification, or ballot power.
